pollutant_keys: canonical: upper case without '.', '_', '-' or spaces (PM2.5 -> PM25)
general_caveats: Backgrounds are single-hour regional values for the scenario hour, from monitors upwind of the city where possible; they are not design values.
NAAQS levels are statistical forms over months to years; one modelled hour cannot show compliance or exceedance, so they are reference levels only.

SO2.label: SO₂
SO2.conversion: ug/m3 = ppb x MW / 24.45 (25 degC, 1 atm); MW = 64.066 g/mol

naaqs.form: 99th percentile of daily maximum 1-hour values, averaged over 3 years

SO2.naaqs_text: 75 ppb, 1-hour (99th percentile of daily 1-h maxima, 3-yr average)
SO2.note: Mostly primary. A stored unit field (conserved tracer) maps directly onto SO2 over a single hour; conversion to sulfate is slow (percent per hour) and is ignored.

CO.label: CO
CO.conversion: ug/m3 = ppm x 1000 x MW / 24.45 (25 degC, 1 atm); MW = 28.010 g/mol

naaqs.form: not to be exceeded more than once per year
not to be exceeded more than once per year

CO.naaqs_text: 35 ppm, 1-hour; 9 ppm, 8-hour (not to be exceeded more than once per year)
CO.note: Primary and nearly inert over an hour, so the tracer field applies directly.
caveats: No rural or suburban CO monitor is in range, so CO backgrounds come from urban neighbourhood monitors and include local traffic.

NO2.label: NO₂
NO2.conversion: ug/m3 = ppb x MW / 24.45 (25 degC, 1 atm); MW = 46.005 g/mol

naaqs.form: 98th percentile of daily maximum 1-hour values, averaged over 3 years

NO2.naaqs_text: 100 ppb, 1-hour (98th percentile of daily 1-h maxima, 3-yr average); 53 ppb annual
NO2.note: Partly secondary: sources emit mostly NO, which ozone converts to NO2. The unit field is a conserved tracer, so a student's NOx plume is not an NO2 plume; adding the tracer to this NO2 background overstates NO2 near sources unless a conversion (for example a fixed NO2/NOx ratio such as Appendix W's ARM2 range 0.5-0.9) is applied. The background itself already includes secondary NO2 formed upwind.
caveats: The app counts all emitted NOx as NO2 (the tracer upper limit); real near-source NO2 is lower because sources emit mostly NO.
Partly secondary: the background already includes NO2 formed upwind.

PM25.label: PM₂.₅
PM25.conversion: measured in ug/m3 (local conditions); no conversion

naaqs.form: annual mean, averaged over 3 years (2024 revision)

PM25.note: Mixed primary and secondary (sulfate, nitrate, organics formed in the atmosphere). The tracer field represents primary PM2.5 only; the background carries the regional secondary part.
caveats: The tracer represents primary PM2.5 only; the background carries the regional secondary part (sulfate, nitrate, organics).

O3.label: O₃
O3.conversion: ug/m3 = ppb x MW / 24.45 (25 degC, 1 atm); MW = 47.998 g/mol

naaqs.form: annual fourth-highest daily maximum 8-hour value, averaged over 3 years

O3.naaqs_text: 70 ppb, 8-hour (annual fourth-highest daily maximum 8-h average, 3-yr average)
O3.note: Entirely secondary: formed from NOx and VOC in sunlight and destroyed by fresh NO near sources (titration). No catalogue source emits ozone, and the linear unit fields cannot represent its chemistry; the value is the regional background for the linearity module (Agent G). At night and in the morning, ozone inside the city is usually lower than this upwind regional value because of titration (hypothesis to keep in mind when comparing).
caveats: Secondary pollutant: ozone is not emitted, so it is not a tracer and the linear engine does not apply (see the linearity module).
